name: Massachusetts

steps.detail: Massachusetts has no athlete agent law. A bill that would have required one (H1930) was sent to study on March 26, 2026.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Many schools have their own agent sign-up, for example UMass and Holy Cross.

steps.text: Warn the athlete in writing that signing could affect their eligibility
steps.detail: This is required by federal law (SPARTA) in every state.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Federal law bans pre-dating or post-dating it.

steps.text: High school athletes: make sure they give their school a copy of your agreement
Never make false promises or give gifts or money to recruit athletes
steps.detail: This is a federal SPARTA rule.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. Not yet law.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap fees at 5% and create public agent databases.

watch_list.status: Sent to study on March 26, 2026 (H5281). It could come back next session.
watch_list.impact: It would require agent registration and cap fees at 15%.

review_notes: The SPARTA requirements were taken from a secondary summary. They should be checked against 15 U.S.C. 7801-7807.
